## Threat Model

### System context

MD4C is a C library (src/md4c.c, md4c.h, md4c-html.c, md4c-html.h, entity.c, entity.h) that parses CommonMark-style Markdown from a caller-supplied byte buffer and calls back into the host application, plus an HTML renderer built on it. It is embedded as a library, not a network service. Untrusted Markdown input is the primary data entering the process, and the library's callers decide whether that input is trusted. Build and CI are CMake plus Travis/AppVeyor with -Werror and coverage. No dependency manifests, no API contract artefacts and no runtime configuration were present in the snapshot.

### Assets

| Asset | Sensitivity | Description |
|---|---|---|
| host process memory | high | Heap and stack of the embedding application that md4c parses into; memory-safety failures here are the main impact. |
| parser availability | medium | Ability of the host to parse untrusted input in bounded time and memory. |
| rendered HTML output | medium | HTML produced by md_html(); correctness and escaping affect downstream consumers. |

### Trust boundaries

- **md_parse() input buffer (src/md4c.c)** — untrusted Markdown bytes -&gt; parser internals → host process memory, parser availability
- **md_html() input and callback (src/md4c-html.c)** — untrusted Markdown -&gt; HTML renderer output → rendered HTML output, host process memory

### Ranked threats

| ID | Threat | Actor | Surface | Asset | Impact | Likelihood | Controls | Investigation unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Crafted Markdown causes out-of-bounds read or write in the parser, leading to memory corruption in the host process. | remote_unauth | md_parse() input buffer (src/md4c.c) | host process memory | high | rare | Fuzzing history and bounds-fix commits (0.3.0 entity bounds, 0.3.3 fuzz fix); no sanitizer evidence in snapshot. | minted |
| T2 | Use-after-free or double-free in parser block/span tree or ref-def hashtable handling on crafted input. | remote_unauth | md_parse() input buffer (src/md4c.c) | host process memory | high | rare | none evident in structural snapshot; source not read. | minted |
| T3 | Integer overflow in size computation before allocation in parser or HTML renderer yields undersized buffer and heap overflow. | remote_unauth | md_parse() input buffer (src/md4c.c) | host process memory | high | rare | unknown; source not inspected. | minted |
| T4 | Attacker-controlled text used as a printf-style format string in parser or renderer diagnostics. | remote_unauth | md_html() input and callback (src/md4c-html.c) | host process memory | high | very_rare | HTML renderer writes output via callbacks rather than printf-family calls with input; not confirmed. | minted |
| T6 | Input reaches a shell via system() or exec() in the library or its md2html driver. | remote_unauth | md_html() input and callback (src/md4c-html.c) | host process memory | high | very_rare | library has no process-spawning code by design; not confirmed in source. | minted |
| T5 | Race or TOCTOU between size check and use in shared parser state when the library is used from multiple threads. | local_user | md_parse() input buffer (src/md4c.c) | host process memory | medium | very_rare | parser state is per-call; no shared globals seen in structure. | minted |
| T7 | Entity lookup in entity.c reads past the end of its table on crafted entity names, leaking adjacent memory into rendered output. | remote_unauth | md_html() input and callback (src/md4c-html.c) | rendered HTML output | medium | rare | Bounds fix for md_is_entity_str per CHANGELOG 0.3.0; current code not read. | minted |
